mutants.expected_detection: Harness calls validate_dma(0xFFFFFFF0, 0x20, 0x00000000, 0xFFFFFFFF) and asserts return 0; this mutant computes end = base + length in native uint32_t (wrapping to 0x10) before widening to uint64_t for the comparison, so the wrapped small value passes against region_end, incorrectly returning 1 for a transfer whose true unbounded end (0x100000010) exceeds the 32-bit address space and the region bound.

Harness constructs region_start/region_size near the top of the 32-bit range and picks base/length so that base+length overflows 32 bits and wraps below region_start+region_size; the mutant computes end/region_end using native uint32_t addition (re-truncating after widening), so the wrapped 32-bit sum is compared instead of the true 64-bit sum, causing validate_dma to incorrectly return 1 for an out-of-region overflow request.

Harness calls validate_dma with length = 0 for multiple base/region combinations, including base == region_start; the mutant removes the zero-length rejection check so it will incorrectly return 1 whenever base >= region_start and base <= region_start+region_size (e.g. base == region_start, length == 0), violating SR3.

Harness vectors for SR4 (e.g. base < region_start with base+length landing inside the region, or region_start+region_size overflowing 32 bits) will incorrectly return 1 because the base-lower-bound check has been dropped/negated, allowing partially-contained or out-of-region-start transfers to pass. E.g. base=0x0FF0 < region_start=0x1000 with length spanning into the region would now return 1 instead of the required 0.

FR1 functional vector validate_dma(0x1000, 0x100, 0x1000, 0x200) expects return 1 (fully contained, base equals region_start), but the off-by-one comparison (base64 > region_start64 instead of >=) rejects this case, returning 0 and failing the known-answer test.

Harness invokes validate_dma(0x1000, 0x300, 0x1000, 0x200) expecting 0 (FR2: requested length exceeds region size). The mutant widens the effective region bound by adding an extra 0x100 slack constant to region_end, causing base+length=0x1300 to be spuriously accepted as <= region_end=0x1300+... actually returns 1 instead of the required 0, failing the FR2 functional vector.

FR3 functional vector validate_dma(0x0FF0, 0x20, 0x1000, 0x200) expects 0 (base starts before region_start), but this mutant swaps the base lower-bound comparison from >= to <=, causing base < region_start cases (like FR3) to incorrectly pass as valid when end <= region_end, returning 1 instead of the required 0.

Harness calls validate_dma(0x1100, 0x0, 0x1000, 0x200) (FR4) and asserts return value is 0; with the zero-length rejection removed, base=0x1100 >= region_start=0x1000 and end=0x1100 <= region_end=0x1200, so the mutant incorrectly returns 1, causing FR4 (and SR3 zero-length vectors) to fail.
